chapter: Sunset Cafe, Pass in Review and rebuilding the band
title: Segregation ends the Pass in Review tour and Armstrong calls
summary: Because Black and white performers could not share a stage in the South, the show dumped them; then Armstrong, courted by both Mezzrow and Glaser as manager, contacted Randolph.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, at this time, this was 'way before Martin Luther King had had his walk.

Had had that demonstrations. So everything was tight then, segregated, you see. So they didn't allow the blacks and the whites to be on the stage together. So therefore the show had to go South and they had to dump us. So here's what happened. Then I think -- I believe Louis contacted -- either Louis -- yeah, Louis contacted me. That was two people were trying to be the manager for Louis. Do you know Mezzrow?
